title: A self-correcting variable-metric algorithm framework for nonsmooth optimization
contribution: SVANO: a variable-metric framework for locally Lipschitz minimization. BFGS updates are damped toward a fixed matrix H so that curvature bounds hold for all k, and BFGS self-correction then gives bounded matrices on a fraction p of iterations. This yields generic stationarity theory, a full proof for a convex bundle trust-region instance, and a C++ code with BFGS, bundle and gradient-sampling instances (arXiv v5, pp. 5-20).
problem_entry: Earlier nonsmooth variable-metric methods either restrict updates so matrices stay bounded in all iterations (Curtis-Que) or run unadulterated BFGS, which lacks general guarantees and may break down in the line search before any stationarity guarantee (p. 3).
key_idea: Keep the BFGS formula and a free y_k, but use v_k = beta_k H s_k + (1 - beta_k) y_k with fixed H, so that eta <= s'v/||s||^2 and ||v||^2/s'v <= theta hold for all k; self-correction (tr - ln det) then gives good matrices on at least ceil(pK) of K iterations, enough for convergence (pp. 6, 8, 10).
assumptions: f bounded below, locally Lipschitz, C1 on an open full-measure set (Assumption 2.1, p. 4); convex f for the complete bundle theory (Theorem 4.1, p. 14); weak lower semismoothness for nonconvex line searches (p. 16); classical BFGS instance covered only if stepsizes stay >= alpha_min (p. 12).
proof_devices: potential psi(H) = tr(H) - ln det(H) with trace/determinant recurrences (3.2)-(3.4), after Byrd-Nocedal (p. 9)
Theorem 3.1: good cosines and Rayleigh quotients on at least ceil(pK) of any K iterations, proof by bounding the ceil(pK) smallest loss terms zeta_k (p. 10; App. C pp. 24-25)
Theorem 3.2: decrease on the good subsequence forces ||G w + gamma|| -> 0 and ||s|| -> 0 (p. 11)
Theorem 3.3: practical version of Kiwiel's lemma, stationarity from vanishing convex combinations of eps_k-subgradients (p. 11)
Moreau-Yosida regularization lemmas adapted from Ruszczynski 7.4 for the variable-metric bundle step (pp. 14, 25-27)
Theorem 4.1: radius update tied to a computable stationarity test, delta_k -> 0 proved via the angle between t_k and gamma_k (pp. 14-15)
dual of the trust-region subproblem: affine equality plus bounds, warm start by appending a zero variable (pp. 7-8)
experiments: C++ code with own active-set QP solver; first 10 Haarala et al. problems, n = 50 (5 convex); common W1 = I and y_k for all instances; success = theory test (5.1); counters #iter/#func/#grad/#subs; Bundle and GS stationary on 10/10, BFGS on 1/10 (Table 2, p. 18); ablation theta = infinity: Bundle 5 and GS 4 failures (Table 3, p. 19); LMBM and HANSO at defaults, 'difficult to compare' (pp. 19-20); randomized GS single runs (p. 17); no CPU times.
positioning: Places itself among restricted-update quasi-Newton methods but exploiting self-correction (p. 3); builds on Byrd-Nocedal, Kiwiel, Schramm-Zowe, Ruszczynski and own Curtis-Que and 2016 stochastic self-correcting work (pp. 3, 5, 8, 9, 14, 16); stresses it does not claim classical BFGS cannot be proved convergent (p. 12).
writing: Contribution sentence in abstract (p. 2); open hedging ('The hope is', 'We conjecture', pp. 3, 18); classical BFGS failure shown first to motivate (p. 12); each table explained through a named inequality ((5.2), (C.4), pp. 18-19).
limits_future: Complete proof only for the convex bundle instance (p. 14); nonconvex instances without complete analysis (p. 15); L-BFGS omitted on an unshown observation (p. 20); 10 problems at n = 50, single runs of a randomized method, theta = 20 with large impact (p. 17); future: unbounded or extended-real-valued f (p. 20).

success defined by own theory-based termination test (5.1), though f(x_end) is printed and the gap is conceded for SVANO-BFGS; declines to rank against LMBM/HANSO

title: Inexact sequential quadratic optimization with penalty parameter updates within the QP solver
contribution: A penalty-SQP method that updates the exact-penalty parameter inside a single inexact (matrix-free) QP solve, by ratio tests on primal reductions against dual bounds (DUST) plus a posterior check (PSST). The update is proved to trigger finitely often per subproblem, with global convergence to KKT points, infeasible stationary points or MFCQ-failure points; prototype results on feasible, infeasible and 13 large CUTEr problems (arXiv v3, pp. 2-29).
problem_entry: SQP falters at scale because QPs must be solved accurately; inexact SQP exists but its practical efficiency is open; prior penalty updates happen in hindsight or at the cost of several subproblem solves per iteration, as in the authors' own SQuID (two exact QPs) and [8] (two inexact QPs) (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Track primal-dual estimates for the penalty QP and a dual estimate for the feasibility QP; reduce rho when the penalty-model ratio and complementarity ratio pass but the feasibility ratio fails (DUST), with margins omega_k -> 0; drop rho f(x_k) from the model and keep rho only in the dual objective so dual feasibility survives updates (pp. 5-9, 14).
assumptions: f, c C1 (p. 3); H_rho positive definite for all rho in [0, rho_{k-1}], nonzero constraint gradients (Assumption 1, p. 6); solver iterates feasible and no worse than zero (Assumption 2, p. 11); compact X with 0 interior, bounded derivatives, uniform eigenvalue bounds, bounded multipliers (Assumption 7, pp. 15-16); primal convergence only, no local rate (p. 15).
proof_devices: weak/strong duality ratio certificates: passing r_v or r_phi implies a fixed fraction of the exact model reduction ((3.7)-(3.8), p. 8)
Lipschitz-in-rho bounds on primal and dual subproblem values (Lemma 5, p. 12)
Theorem 6: explicit threshold rho-tilde (3.15) below which DUST never triggers, by contradiction (pp. 13-14)
shifted penalty phi = rho(f - f_low) + v monotone as rho decreases (Lemma 11, p. 17)
Theorem 14: if rho -> 0, limit points are all feasible or all infeasible, via monotone shifted penalty (pp. 18-19)
three-case argument (Lemma 15) and dual form of MFCQ to show feasible limits with rho -> 0 violate MFCQ (Theorem 17, pp. 19-23)
O(n + l) dual coordinate descent via maintained running sums (pp. 25-26)
experiments: Python prototype; 126 CUTEr HS problems with exact modified Hessian: 115/126 vs SQuID 110/122 with SQuID numbers copied from [3] under a different termination test (Table 1, p. 27); sensitivity omega_0 and beta_phi (113, 111 solved) (p. 27); per-problem Hessian-constant changes (p. 28); hs_inf by adding x1 <= 0 and x1 >= 1: 116/126 vs 111/123 (Table 2, p. 28); 13 large CUTEr problems with L-BFGS, failures 'not shown', attempted set unspecified (pp. 28-29); SQuID none in 10 minutes, max 64 s, Ipopt a couple of seconds on LUKVLE10 (p. 29).
positioning: Continues SQuID [3] and inexact SQO [8], restating their QP counts; groups Burke, Han, Han-Mangasarian as hindsight updates and SQuID, Byrd-Lopez-Calva-Nocedal, Byrd-Nocedal-Waltz as multi-solve steering (p. 2); credits Ipopt's two decades of development (p. 29).
writing: Three bullet contributions and the claim 'We prove that our algorithm does not reduce the penalty parameter unnecessarily' (p. 2); intuitive case analysis before proofs (pp. 9-10); 'outperforms' on counts over different sets (pp. 27-28); small slips in percentages, section list and a 'Theorem 15(iv)' reference (pp. 2, 22, 27).
limits_future: Needs a more efficient QP solver and more robust handling of Hessian ill-conditioning (p. 30); coordinate descent weak on ill-conditioned QPs (p. 27); large-scale failures deferred (p. 28); unstated: rival not re-run, no local analysis, per-problem constant changes (pp. 27-28).

coauthors: James V. Burke, Hao Wang, Jiashan Wang

quotes.text: This strategy represents a stark contrast to previously proposed techniques that only update the penalty parameter after a sequence of iterations, in hindsight at the end of an iteration [1, 9, 10], or at the expense of numerous subproblem solves within a single iteration [3, 5, 7].
(On a contemporary laptop to computer, the state-of-the-art code Ipopt [17] solves problem LUKVLE10 in only a couple of seconds, but that code benefits from two decades of software development.)

title: Sequential quadratic optimization for nonlinear equality constrained stochastic optimization
contribution: A line-search-free SQP for equality-constrained problems: first a deterministic twin with Lipschitz-based (adaptive) stepsizes matching line-search SQP theory, then a stochastic-gradient SQP with projected adaptive stepsizes. It gets SG-type expectation guarantees conditioned on a good merit-parameter event, with the bad events shown to have probability zero or to need extreme noise, and beats a heavily tuned stochastic subgradient penalty method on 49 CUTE problems (arXiv v1, pp. 2-28).
problem_entry: Deterministic equality constraints with a stochastic objective; existing stochastic methods are penalty-based and Frank-Wolfe needs convex constraints, while the state-of-the-art line-search SQP is unusable because line searches are intractable (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Replace the line search by minimizing a Lipschitz upper bound of the l1 merit change (three cases around the kink at alpha = 1), keep the model-reduction merit-parameter rule, and in the stochastic version project the adaptive stepsize into an interval of width theta*beta^2 set by an adaptive lower estimate xi (pp. 6-8, 14-16).
assumptions: f C1 with Lipschitz bounded gradient, c with Lipschitz gradients, LICQ via singular values bounded away from zero (Assumption 1, p. 4); H_k bounded and positive definite on null(J_k) (Assumption 4, p. 5); unbiased gradients with variance <= M (Assumption 19, p. 13); known Lipschitz constants and bounded iterates in the analysis, 'admittedly not ideal' (Remark 20, p. 14); event E_tau,small (Assumption 27, p. 20).
proof_devices: tangential/normal decomposition d = u + v and critical quantity Psi_k with index sets K_u, K_v (pp. 8-10)
merit upper bound with kink term |1 - alpha| and three-case sufficient decrease (Lemmas 13-14, pp. 10-11)
merit parameter eventually constant (Lemma 16, p. 12) and xi eventually constant, bounded below deterministically (Lemma 22, p. 16)
standard backtracking SQP analysed in the same lemma sequence for comparison (pp. 4, 8-13)
stepsize interval of width theta*beta^2 (Lemma 23, p. 16) and key merit bound (Lemma 24, pp. 16-18)
expectation of adaptive stepsize times error bounded by splitting on the sign of g'(dbar - d) (Lemma 28, pp. 20-21)
event split E_tau,small / E_tau,big / E_tau,0 with probability-zero (Prop. 33, Example 34) and bounded-noise (Prop. 35) arguments (pp. 20, 24-26)
experiments: Matlab; 49 of 123 CUTE equality problems kept by f non-constant, n + m <= 1000 and LICQ at all iterates of all runs (p. 26); deterministic: Dolan-More profiles of iterations and function evaluations, adaptive as reliable but less efficient, stepsize <1/=1/>1 in 40.9/41.8/17.3 % (pp. 26-27); stochastic: Gaussian noise at 4 levels, 10 runs, 490 instances per level; subgradient baseline tuned per instance over 11 tau values with 10x iterations (110x total); shared L and Gamma, H_k = I for fairness; errors measured with true gradient and least-squares multipliers; box plots (p. 28, not readable); event held in 99.10-99.92 % of iterations (pp. 26-28).
positioning: Line-search SQP on an exact penalty as state of the art (p. 3); penalty and augmented Lagrangian methods criticized (p. 2); ML-venue stochastic penalty methods and stochastic Frank-Wolfe set aside (p. 3); results of the type of SG theory in Bottou-Curtis-Nocedal (pp. 3, 24); analysis follows own inexact SQP papers [4, 5] (p. 8).
writing: Expectation management ('as should be expected, it is sometimes less efficient', p. 3; 'We do not claim', p. 26); explicit admissions (Remark 20, p. 14; theta = 0 'detrimental in practice', p. 24); a section titled 'Poor Merit Parameter Behavior' (p. 24); strongest claim 'consistently and significantly outperforms' rests on box plots (pp. 3, 28).
limits_future: LICQ, bounded iterates, known Lipschitz constants in analysis vs estimates near x0 in practice, results conditional on E_tau,small (pp. 4, 14, 20, 27); unstated: test set filtered on run outcomes (p. 26), inequality constraints not covered; future: theta = 0 variant to drop the bounded-gradient need (p. 28).
